intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

selected_hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Street Food Tour in Centro Histórico
experiences.description: Explore the bustling streets of Mexico City's historic center sampling iconic local dishes such as tacos de canasta, tlayudas, tamales, and fresh aguas frescas from street vendors and traditional market stalls. A guided or self-guided walk through Mercado San Juan and surrounding streets offers an authentic taste of chilango food culture.

experiences.name: Visit the National Museum of Anthropology
experiences.description: Discover one of the world's greatest museums dedicated to pre-Columbian heritage and Mexican culture. Marvel at the iconic Aztec Sun Stone, Mayan artifacts, and exhibits spanning thousands of years of Mesoamerican civilization. The museum is set within the beautiful Bosque de Chapultepec park.

experiences.name: Cooking Class in Coyoacán
experiences.description: Join a hands-on traditional Mexican cooking class in the charming bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán. Learn to prepare classic dishes like mole, chiles en nogada, and handmade tortillas using fresh ingredients sourced from the local Mercado de Coyoacán. A deeply immersive cultural and culinary experience.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born, lived, and created her legendary artwork. Explore her personal belongings, studio, vibrant garden, and rotating exhibitions that celebrate her life, art, and the rich cultural tapestry of Mexico. A must-see cultural landmark in the heart of Coyoacán.

experiences.name: Xochimilco Trajinera Boat Ride and Local Food Market
experiences.description: Glide through the ancient Aztec canals of Xochimilco on a colorful trajinera (flat-bottomed boat). Enjoy local snacks and drinks sold by vendors on passing boats, listen to mariachi music, and soak in the festive atmosphere. Visit the nearby Mercado Xochimilco for fresh local produce and traditional antojitos.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Centro Histórico via Metro Line 5 to Pantitlán, then transfer to Line 2 toward Tasqueña, exit at Zócalo station (approx. 45–60 min, under $1 USD). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed first walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the massive main square and heart of the city. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry) and the National Palace exterior with its famous Diego Rivera murals visible just inside the entrance (free). Get your bearings and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Madero Street, a pedestrian avenue lined with historic buildings, street performers, and vendors. Head to the nearby Mercado de Artesanías or simply explore the lively Centro streets. Wind down with dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a quick coffee and pan dulce from a street bakery near the airport or hotel (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Grab tacos al pastor or quesadillas from a street stand near the Zócalo (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (budget-friendly traditional Mexican dishes) or a local fondita (small family restaurant) near Centro Histórico — try sopa de lima and enchiladas (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use the Mexico City Metro — it's one of the cheapest in the world at about 5 MXN (~$0.25 USD) per ride. Get a rechargeable Metro card at the airport or any station. Keep valuables secure in busy Centro areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor (ancient Aztec temple ruins) right next to the Zócalo. Entry is around $4 USD and includes the excellent on-site museum. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the excavated ruins and artifacts that tell the story of the Mexica civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (Palace of Fine Arts) — the exterior and ground-floor lobby are free to admire. Then walk through Alameda Central park, a beautiful green space perfect for people-watching. Visit the Museo Mural Diego Rivera nearby (entry ~$2 USD) to see his famous mural 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Park.'
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Dolores Street, just off Alameda — a quirky and photogenic block. Then head back toward Centro for dinner and an evening walk along the illuminated Zócalo, which is especially beautiful after dark.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole from a street cart near the hotel — a classic Mexico City breakfast (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Tortas or tlayudas from a market stall near Alameda Central (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Mercado San Juan (Mercado de Medina) — browse food stalls for fresh seafood tostadas, tacos, and aguas frescas (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with the Chapultepec visit on Day 3. Comfortable walking shoes are essential — you'll cover 5–8 km on foot today.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 1, Chapultepec station) to Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world. Walk through the park and visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle) — entry is ~$3 USD. The castle offers stunning panoramic views of the city and houses the National History Museum inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) within Chapultepec Park — entry is ~$5 USD. This is a must-see for culture lovers, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and artifacts from all of Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations. Plan at least 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Condesa or Roma neighborhoods (nearby Metro stops) for an evening walk. Browse the tree-lined streets, street art, and local boutiques. These neighborhoods have a great atmosphere without needing to spend much.

meals.breakfast: Chilaquiles or huevos rancheros at a local fondita near the hotel (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the food stalls or small restaurants near Chapultepec park entrance — try a torta ahogada or elote (corn on the cob with toppings) (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Mercado Medellín in Colonia Roma — a vibrant local market with food stalls serving regional Mexican dishes and fresh produce (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum is massive — pick up a free map at the entrance and prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls if time is limited. The park itself is free and great for a picnic. Avoid carrying large bags or displaying expensive electronics in the park.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — take a bus from Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Line 5, Terminal Aérea, then bus station) to the ancient pyramids (~$3–4 USD each way, 1 hour). Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead (~$5 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the on-site museum included with entry. Browse the local artisan market near the exit for affordable souvenirs (bargaining is expected). Head back to Mexico City by bus in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and relax. Visit the Plaza Garibaldi, the famous mariachi square, just north of Centro — free to enter and watch musicians perform. Have dinner in the area and enjoy the lively night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the bus terminal — a torta or pastry (~$2–3 USD) before departing early
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the small restaurants just outside the Teotihuacán site — try mole or barbacoa with handmade tortillas (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Pozolería near Plaza Garibaldi or a taquería on Calle República de Uruguay — hearty pozole rojo or green enchiladas (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Leave for Teotihuacán by 8:00–8:30 AM to make the most of the day and avoid midday heat. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water — the site is entirely outdoors with little shade. Wear sturdy shoes for pyramid climbing. Buses depart frequently from Terminal del Norte.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the historic neighborhood of Coyoacán via Metro (Line 3, Coyoacán station or Viveros). Explore the colorful Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo — the famous 'Casa Azul' (Blue House) — entry ~$8–10 USD (book online in advance as it sells out). This is one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Coyoacán's bohemian streets and artisan market (Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán) for affordable crafts and souvenirs. Visit the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán food hall for a final taste of local cuisine. Head back to Centro Histórico to pack and prepare for departure or next destination.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening stroll around the Zócalo and Madero Street. Pick up any last souvenirs from street vendors (look for handmade crafts, Lucha Libre masks, and local sweets like cajeta or tamarind candies). Enjoy a farewell dinner in Centro.

meals.breakfast: Café de olla (traditional spiced coffee) and pan dulce at a local panadería in Centro (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas at Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — one of the best budget food experiences in the city (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a traditional pulquería or cantina in Centro Histórico — try pulque (traditional fermented drink) alongside tacos de canasta or chiles en nogada if in season (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online at museofridakahlo.org.mx as soon as possible. Coyoacán is about 45 minutes from Centro by Metro and is very walkable once you arrive. This is a great neighborhood to spend a relaxed final morning before any onward travel.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approximately 45–60 min by metro or Uber). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the heart of Mexico City. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace from the outside. Stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the colonial architecture and street life.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero and the nearby Alameda Central park at dusk. Enjoy the illuminated historic buildings and local atmosphere before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport on arrival day)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and authentic meal at a local fondita or mercado stall near the Zócalo — try a comida corrida (set lunch menu) for around 80–120 MXN at Mercado San Juan or a nearby side street eatery.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de Tacuba, a historic and mid-range restaurant just steps from the hotel in Centro Histórico. Try classic Mexican dishes like mole enchiladas or chiles en nogada in a beautifully tiled colonial setting.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts post-arrival. Keep the pace relaxed to recover from travel. Exchange currency at a reputable casa de cambio near the Zócalo rather than at the airport for better rates. Uber is recommended over taxis for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor, located directly behind the Metropolitan Cathedral. Explore the ruins of the ancient Aztec temple and the excellent on-site museum with artifacts from the Mexica civilization. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) on the Zócalo to view Diego Rivera's magnificent murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mercado de Artesanías or browse the historic streets around República de Uruguay for local crafts and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Barrio de Tepito border or stay in Centro to experience the lively evening street food scene. Visit the area around Plaza Garibaldi to hear Mariachi bands perform in the open air — a quintessential Mexico City experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby café such as El Cardenal (Centro branch) — try chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla for an authentic morning meal (150–200 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a comida corrida spot on Calle Moneda or República de Brasil near the Templo Mayor — a full three-course meal with agua fresca for around 100–130 MXN.
meals.dinner: Tacos and street food around Plaza Garibaldi — try tacos de canasta, quesadillas, and elotes from local vendors. Budget around 100–150 MXN for a satisfying spread.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor charges approximately 90 MXN entry. The Palacio Nacional is free. Plaza Garibaldi is lively after 20:00 — stay aware of your surroundings and keep valuables secure.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or Uber to Coyoacán (about 30–40 min from Centro). Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly. Explore the iconic blue house and learn about Frida Kahlo's life and art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the charming streets of Coyoacán village, browse the weekend artisan market in Jardín Centenario, and visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky for a dose of 20th-century political history. Enjoy the bohemian, tree-lined neighborhood atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico or head to the neighboring Roma/Condesa neighborhood for a more modern evening scene. Explore the tree-lined streets, independent bookshops, and café culture of Colonia Roma.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Coyoacán at Café El Jarocho, a legendary local coffee stand — grab a café de olla and a pastry for under 60 MXN while soaking up neighborhood life.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — a mid-range restaurant with excellent modern Mexican cuisine, mezcal selection, and a lovely courtyard. Budget around 300–400 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Colonia Roma at Contramar (arrive early or book ahead) for world-famous Mexican seafood, or try a more casual option like El Tizoncito, the birthplace of tacos al pastor, for a budget-friendly evening meal (150–200 MXN).

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets at least 2–3 days in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Entry is approximately 270 MXN. Coyoacán is especially lively and atmospheric on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or organized tour (about 50 min) to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early (gates open at 09:00) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop at the Basílica de Guadalupe in northern Mexico City on the way back — one of the most visited Catholic shrines in the world, with fascinating history and architecture (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Back in Centro Histórico, explore the atmospheric streets around Calle Regina and the pedestrian corridor — a hub of local bars, mezcalerías, and casual eateries popular with locals.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab tamales and atole from a street cart near the hotel or eat a quick meal at the hotel (budget 80–120 MXN).
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the restaurants near the Teotihuacán site entrance — try La Gruta, a restaurant set inside a natural cave/grotto near the pyramids, for a memorable mid-range dining experience (250–350 MXN per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezcalería on Calle Regina such as Bosforo or a similar spot — enjoy small plates (botanas) like tlayudas, chapulines (grasshoppers), and queso Oaxaqueño paired with artisanal mezcal. Budget 250–350 MXN including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán entry is approximately 90 MXN. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable shoes — the pyramids involve significant climbing and sun exposure. Carry water. Uber to Teotihuacán costs roughly 300–400 MXN each way; shared tours from Centro are available for around 300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City's stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco cultural palace. View the Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros murals inside (entry to murals approximately 90 MXN). Spend time in the surrounding Alameda Central park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) nearby for an overview of Mexican art from the colonial period to the 20th century (entry approximately 90 MXN). Afterward, do a final stroll through the Centro Histórico — browse bookstores on Donceles street (the 'street of used books'), and pick up last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Centro Histórico to celebrate the trip. Enjoy a relaxed final evening walk around the illuminated Zócalo and cathedral before heading back to the hotel to pack.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at El Cardenal (Centro branch) — a beloved local institution. Try the hot chocolate with churros, enfrijoladas, or huevos rancheros. Budget around 180–250 MXN.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Mercado San Juan — an upscale covered market with a wide variety of food stalls offering everything from fresh seafood tostadas to international bites and local cheeses. Budget 150–200 MXN.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Azul Histórico, a refined yet mid-range Mexican restaurant in the Centro Histórico with a beautiful open courtyard. Try regional Mexican specialties like cochinita pibil or mole negro. Budget 350–500 MXN per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Confirm return transfer or airport Uber in advance. March weather in Mexico City is typically mild and dry (18–24°C), ideal for walking — light layers recommended for evenings.

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Benito Juárez International Airport to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Centro Histórico: explore the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), marvel at the Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site with a dedicated expert guide who provides deep cultural and historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico at dusk, visiting the Palacio de Bellas Artes exterior and the iconic Librería El Péndulo for a cultural aperitif. End the evening with a curated mezcal tasting at a premium mezcalería.

meals.lunch: Casual welcome lunch at Azul Histórico — a refined Mexican cuisine restaurant set in a stunning colonial courtyard within Centro Histórico, offering regional dishes and fresh agua frescas.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar (reservation required) or Casa de Sierra Nevada pop-up dining — enjoy elevated Mexican seafood and contemporary tasting menus with sommelier-selected wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Templo Mayor hours (typically closes at 17:00). Book dinner reservations at least 48 hours ahead. Stay hydrated — altitude in Mexico City is approximately 2,240 meters.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Palacio Nacional to admire Diego Rivera's monumental murals depicting Mexican history — arrive early for an uncrowded experience. Follow with a guided tour of the National Museum of Anthropology (Museo Nacional de Antropología) in Chapultepec, one of the world's greatest cultural museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) with a private guide, enjoying panoramic views over the city. Afterward, take a leisurely walk through the Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's grand urban park, stopping at the Lago de Chapultepec.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Polanco neighborhood for an evening of luxury boutique browsing on Presidente Masaryk Avenue, followed by cocktails at a rooftop bar with skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at your boutique hotel or at Café de Tacuba — a historic 1912 restaurant in Centro Histórico serving traditional Mexican breakfast dishes in a beautifully tiled colonial setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quintonil in Polanco — one of Latin America's top restaurants, Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated venue showcasing indigenous Mexican ingredients in innovative tasting menus.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's world-renowned flagship restaurant offering the iconic Mole Madre tasting menu, a pinnacle of contemporary Mexican haute cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol and Quintonil well in advance — these are among the most sought-after tables in Latin America. Private car or Uber recommended between Centro Histórico, Chapultepec, and Polanco. The National Museum of Anthropology requires at least 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Teotihuacán — depart early by private chauffeured vehicle. Enjoy an exclusive guided tour of the Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, and the Avenue of the Dead before the crowds arrive. Optional: access a private archaeological briefing from a licensed expert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán's lesser-visited Palace of Quetzalpapálotl and the Mica Temple. On the return journey, stop at a traditional artisan workshop in the nearby town of San Juan Teotihuacán to observe obsidian carving and purchase authentic handcrafted pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico refreshed. Enjoy a relaxing evening at your hotel's spa (if available) or a private temazcal (traditional Mexican sweat lodge) experience arranged through a luxury wellness provider.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — request a packed gourmet picnic basket for the journey to Teotihuacán.
meals.lunch: Exclusive lunch at La Gruta Restaurant — a breathtaking dining experience inside a natural cave grotto adjacent to the Teotihuacán site, serving traditional Mexican cuisine with live marimba music.
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at Limosneros in Centro Histórico — a sophisticated restaurant in a 17th-century colonial building, specializing in pre-Hispanic and regional Mexican cuisine with an exceptional mezcal and craft cocktail program.

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 07:00 to arrive at Teotihuacán before peak crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sun protection — the site is largely exposed. The round trip is approximately 90 minutes each way. Book La Gruta in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Xochimilco canals via a decorated trajinera (traditional flat-bottomed boat) — enjoy the UNESCO-listed floating gardens with a private guide, mariachi musicians, and a curated brunch spread on board. Visit the unique Isla de las Muñecas (Island of the Dolls) for a fascinating cultural detour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul / The Blue House) in Coyoacán with a private guide — explore the iconic cobblestone neighborhood of Coyoacán, browsing artisan markets and admiring colonial architecture. Visit the Leon Trotsky Museum nearby for added historical depth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico. Enjoy a private rooftop sunset experience at a luxury hotel terrace (such as the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México rooftop) with panoramic views over the Zócalo and the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Gourmet brunch served on your private trajinera in Xochimilco — curated by a private chef with traditional antojitos, fresh ceviche, guacamole, and regional beverages including micheladas and aguas frescas.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Cardenal in Centro Histórico — a beloved Mexico City institution since 1969, renowned for its impeccably prepared traditional Mexican cuisine, outstanding mole dishes, and exceptional service in an elegant colonial setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets well in advance — entry is limited and sells out quickly. Xochimilco is approximately 45 minutes south of Centro Histórico by private car. Coyoacán is a walkable, charming neighborhood — allow 2–3 hours to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Museo Soumaya in Polanco — one of Mexico's most architecturally striking museums, housing an extraordinary collection of European and Mexican art including works by Rodin, Dalí, and Monet. Follow with a walk through the adjacent Jumex Museum for contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a premium culinary experience: a private Mexican cooking class with a celebrated local chef in a luxury kitchen studio, learning to prepare iconic dishes such as mole negro, chiles en nogada, and traditional tamales. Take home a curated set of local spices and a recipe booklet as a memento.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening farewell: enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a sophisticated bar in Roma Norte or Condesa neighborhood, followed by a grand farewell dinner. End the evening with a nightcap at a jazz bar or live music venue in Colonia Roma.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at Café Nin in Colonia Juárez — a stylish all-day café beloved by Mexico City's creative class, serving French-Mexican fusion breakfasts in a beautifully designed space.
meals.lunch: Light lunch included as part of the cooking class experience — taste everything you prepare with a glass of Mexican wine or artisanal beer.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Sud 777 in Pedregal — Chef Edgar Núñez's celebrated restaurant offering a sophisticated tasting menu rooted in Mexican terroir, with an exceptional natural wine list and impeccable service in a stunning garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class at least 3–4 days in advance. Sud 777 requires a reservation. If departing the following morning, arrange a private transfer and confirm checkout logistics with the hotel. Consider purchasing artisanal mezcal, chocolate, or vanilla as premium gifts to take home.
